'Quite a bit of instability': Entirety of Victoria under thunderstorm threat as the Top End braces for a possibly severe heatwave
The entirety of one state is at risk of possibly severe thunderstorms on Monday as a heatwave scorches the Top End, while other states brace for heavy rain, wind and hail.
The whole state of Victoria is at risk of possibly severe thunderstorms on Monday as a heatwave scorches the Top End.
News24 weather presenter Wendy John warned Victorians that weather “instability” is set to continue with a widespread risk of storms across the state.
“Victoria, well, you've had quite a bit of instability over the last couple of days. That's going to continue throughout Monday,” John said.
“Risk of widespread risk of storms, thunderstorms right throughout the state, possibly intensifying into potentially severe storms around Swan Hill region down to Bendigo about lunchtime, throughout the afternoon.”
On the other hand, Queenslanders were in for more “summertime conditions” after a period of wet weather, though some areas have received flood warnings.
John said places such as Longreach and Birdsville were in for a 41C and 45C Monday.
Meanwhile, along the coast, some rainfall can be expected with some areas possibly catching up to 10 millimetres.
“Last month of spring, New South Wales, you can see a lot of instability coming here from Victoria moving up,” John said.
“You may have chance of some thunderstorms in that, but much less risk than you've had over the weekend.
“Lismore up in the northern rivers, you might be picking up a little bit of that, from Queensland.”
South Australia, however, can prepare for “a lot more sunshine”.
In Western Australia, there are some spots of rain expected in the southwest, but a relatively warm Monday is on the cards, with Kalgoorlie set for 30C and Port Hedland at 38C.
“The further north we go, it's getting pretty hot there,” John said, with the Top End bracing for “severe or high heat wave” warnings.
“So Broome, 33C, but slightly further north, Derby, Kununurra, pushing 40C. Certainly other areas, Alice Springs, 40C, Uluru, very close, Tennant Creek.”
On top of the heat, thunderstorms are also expected with travellers warned of the dynamic weather pattern in the northern regions with the “record-breaking” El Nino event.

Lagos Warns Residents of Extreme Heat Risks as El Niño Strengthens and Dry Season Nears
Lagos State has urged residents to take precautions against extreme heat linked to a strengthening El Niño and the coming dry season, warning of dehydration, respiratory problems and poor air quality, especially for vulnerable groups.
The Lagos State Government has urged residents to take precautions against possible extreme heat as the dry season approaches and the El Niño climate challenge strengthens.
The state Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, issued the warning in a statement shared on X on Sunday. Wahab warned that rising temperatures could worsen dehydration, heat discomfort, respiratory problems and poor air quality, particularly among children, older persons, pregnant women and outdoor workers.

He said: As Lagos prepares for possible extreme heat conditions associated with the strengthening El Niño climate pattern and the transition into the dry season, I urge all residents to take necessary precautions to protect their health and wellbeing. He attributed the state's vulnerability to its high population density, rapid urbanisation, limited green spaces and built-up environment, which can intensify the urban heat effect. As a densely populated and rapidly urbanising coastal city, Lagos is particularly vulnerable to rising temperatures.
Our densely built-up neighbourhoods, roads and limited green spaces can intensify the urban heat effect, making conditions more challenging for many residents. The anticipated conditions could increase heat discomfort, dehydration, respiratory challenges and poor air quality, particularly among vulnerable groups, including children, older persons, pregnant women and outdoor workers, the statement said.
In his advisory, Wahab urged residents to stay hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, wear light clothing and limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours of the day. I therefore call on every Lagos resident, community leader, market association, school, business owner and employer to take this advisory seriously. Let us make access to clean drinking water, shaded spaces and proper ventilation a priority, especially for those who work outdoors and those most at risk.
Precautions against extreme heat advised
Residents are also urged to stay hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, wear light clothing, limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours and avoid open burning of refuse, the statement said. Residents were also advised to avoid open burning of refuse and prioritise access to clean drinking water, shaded areas and proper ventilation, particularly for vulnerable people and outdoor workers. Beyond immediate precautions, we must confront the environmental factors that worsen urban heat.
Protect our trees, plant more, preserve our green spaces, dispose of waste responsibly and desist from activities that degrade our environment, the statement added. It stressed that the government would continue to strengthen public awareness and collaborate with relevant agencies and stakeholders to improve preparedness and response to extreme heat. It added that households, communities and businesses all had a role to play in protecting public health and making Lagos more resilient to climate-related challenges.
Building climate resilience in Lagos
Keeping Lagos safe from the impacts of extreme heat requires action from all of us. Government will continue to strengthen public awareness and collaborate with relevant agencies and stakeholders to improve preparedness and response. But every household, street, community and business has a role to play. Let us act early, look out for one another and take collective responsibility for building a cooler, healthier and more climate-resilient Lagos, the statement said.
El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than normal. El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. The phenomenon does not produce the same effects everywhere, as local weather conditions and other ocean-atmosphere processes can influence its impact.

India’s car sales breach all-time high of 5 lakh units in Oct
Domestic passenger vehicle wholesales breached a record 5-lakh mark in October, driven by a strong festive demand, with leading automakers such as Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai and Mahindra & Mahindra recording their highest-ever monthly sales.
New Delhi, Nov 1 (IANS) Domestic passenger vehicle wholesales breached a record 5-lakh mark in October, driven by a strong festive demand, with leading automakers such as Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai and Mahindra & Mahindra recording their highest-ever monthly sales.
Domestic passenger vehicle wholesale dispatches, comprising cars and SUVs, from factories to retail dealers, which constitute wholesales, are estimated in the range of 5.25-5.3 lakh units in October this year, against 4.6 lakh units in October 2025. This represents a growth of around 13-15 per cent, which comes on top of a high base in the same month last year.
Market leader Maruti Suzuki reported domestic passenger vehicle dispatches of 2.12 lakh units in October, which represents growth of 20 per cent year-on-year. Tata Motors recorded 21 per cent growth to 73,894 units, while M&M posted a 2 per cent rise to record 73,338 units. Hyundai registered a 16.7 per cent increase in domestic wholesales to 62,799 units.
With Dhanteras and Diwali in the first half of November, October wholesales largely reflect dealers stocking up ahead of peak festive deliveries. October registrations, by contrast, are expected to decline against last year's high festive base, as a significant share of festive deliveries shifts into November, said Gaurav Vangaal, associate Director for Light Vehicle Production Forecasting at Mobility Global.
October's growth comes on a high base. In 2025, sales from mid-August to mid-September were subdued as buyers held off purchases, expecting a GST cut. After the lower rates took effect in the last week of September, demand rebounded, driving strong sales through the festive season and into October.
"Strong festive demand, coupled with healthy momentum in both domestic and export markets, helped us set this new sales record," said Hyundai Motor India MD and CEO Tarun Garg.
Mahindra & Mahindra's Automotive business President Velusamy R also noted that October was a landmark month for the company, with the festival season together with a refreshed portfolio keeping the demand strong.
The passenger vehicle industry has maintained robust growth momentum since GST rates were cut last year. Lower borrowing costs have also improved affordability, while recent income tax reforms have left consumers with more money to spend. In the first half of the current financial year, domestic passenger vehicle sales grew 28.3 per cent to 20.55 lakh units.
--IANS

CHENNAI: The Chennai and Tiruvallur district administrations have declared a holiday for all schools and colleges in their respective districts on Monday (November 2) as a precautionary measure in view of Cyclone Murasu. The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has issued an orange alert for Chennai and Tiruvallur districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall across several northern Tamil Nadu districts over the next two days, as Cyclone Murasu moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Meanwhile, the Tamil Nadu Revenue Administration and Disaster Management Department has directed district collectors across the State to remain on high alert and follow standard operating procedures for disaster management.
The Additional Chief Secretary and Commissioner of Revenue Administration has instructed collectors to mobilise administrative machinery and take adequate preparedness measures. Officials have also been asked to maintain strict vigilance and immediately report any untoward incidents to the State Emergency Operations Centre.
According to the IMD's latest bulletin issued at 9.14 pm on Sunday, Cyclone Murasu was moving west-northwestwards at a speed of 27 kmph over the southwest and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal.
At 2.30 pm on November 1, the system was centred about 480 km east-southeast of Chennai, 550 km east-southeast of Nellore, 560 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 600 km southeast of Ongole and 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam.
The weather department said the cyclone is very likely to intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal around the morning of November 2.
It is then expected to move northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur as a severe cyclonic storm, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph, between 11.30 pm on November 2 and 4 am on November 3.
In its rainfall warning bulletin, the RMC has issued an orange alert for Tiruvallur on November 1 and for Chennai and Tiruvallur on November 2, indicating the possibility of very heavy rainfall (12-20 cm in 24 hours).
A yellow alert was issued for Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet and the Nilgiris on November 1, with heavy rainfall likely (7-11 cm).
On November 2, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet, Vellore and the Nilgiris are under a yellow alert for heavy rainfall. On November 3, the warning is confined to isolated heavy rainfall over the Nilgiris.
The RMC has also warned of thunderstorms and lightning accompanied by gusty winds of 40-50 kmph at one or two places in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Kraikal on November 1 and 2. The warning continues for isolated places until November 5.
The weather department has forecast squally winds reaching 55-65 kmph, gusting up to 75 kmph, at isolated places in Tiruvallur, Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet, Vellore, Tiruvannamalai and Villupuram districts, as well as Puducherry, on November 1 and 2.
Winds reaching 40-50 kmph, gusting up to 60 kmph, are also likely at isolated places across the remaining north coastal Tamil Nadu districts.
Meanwhile, explaining the impact of the cyclone on moisture conditions, easterly winds, and rainfall activity, weather blogger Pradeep John, popularly known as Tamil Nadu Weatherman, told DT Next: "Cyclone Arnab had cut off the easterly winds, resulting in dry weather in northern Tamil Nadu and other parts of the State. However, Cyclone Murasu has not disrupted the easterly winds. As the severe cyclonic storm is expected to make landfall near Nellore, rainfall activity is likely to continue across the State over the next few days."
